BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's Draft SPA & Disclosure Letter

Before the substance: a procedural flag. The **"Reviewer Efficiency Note"** instructing us to treat everything marked `[STANDARD]` as pre-cleared and review only `[OPEN]` items is a negotiating device, not a fact. Nothing has been "cleared by both sides." There is not a single `[OPEN]` tag in the package — which means accepting that framing would mean accepting the Seller's entire position unexamined. I have reviewed every clause on its merits. **Do not adopt the Seller's categorisation.**

Here are the material departures from our positions.

---

## 1. General liability cap (Clause 12.1) — TOO LOW
Seller proposes **20% / AUD 4,800,000**. Our starting position is **25% / AUD 6,000,000**. The 20% figure is only a *conditional fallback* requiring prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft — **none has been given**. Push back to 25%. I cannot treat 20% as acceptable.

## 2. Thresholds (Clause 12.2) — FAR TOO HIGH
- De minimis: Seller **AUD 25,000** vs our **AUD 5,000**.
- Basket: Seller **AUD 250,000** vs our **AUD 50,000**.
- Recovery: Seller wants **excess-above-basket only**; we require **first-dollar recovery once the basket is exceeded**.

All three are materially off. Push back on each.

## 3. Time limits (Clause 12.3/13) — TOO SHORT + overreaching sweep
- General claims: Seller **18 months** vs our **24 months**. 18 months is a fallback needing Frost approval — not given. Push to 24 months.
- The "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" default is a trap — it silently sweeps Fundamental/Title/Tax/Fraud into the general regime. **Reverse the default:** limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims; everything else is separately regimed.

## 4. Fundamental / Title warranties — UNACCEPTABLE
Seller wants capacity and title warranties under the **same caps and time limits** as general warranties "for administrative simplicity." This collapses our required separate regime. We require: **100% cap, minimum six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.** Reject outright — this is not an administrative convenience, it is a substantive cap on our core protections.

## 5. Fraud carve-out — MISSING
Nowhere do the Seller's limitation, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance clauses (9.3/12.8/20.5) carve out **fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct**. Clause 1.4 of the Disclosure Letter ("nothing admits breach…") compounds this. We require an express, non-waivable carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Insert it.

## 6. Disclosure framework (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §§1.1–1.2) — REJECT
Seller relies on **whole-data-room deemed disclosure** (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and **public register** disclosure. Our playbook rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. We require **specific, fair disclosure** of each matter with sufficient detail. Strike §§1.1 and 1.2's general sweep.

## 7. Buyer knowledge (Clause 8.3) — REJECT blanket exclusion
Seller excludes any claim the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge" of, **including anything discoverable from the data room or public records**. This is a blanket constructive-knowledge bar — delete it. Any knowledge qualifier must be limited to **actual knowledge of named buyer persons**, and must **never** excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. Note how this interacts with §6: deemed disclosure + deemed knowledge together could neutralise nearly every warranty.

## 8. Bluefen consent (Clause 3/6.3) — INSUFFICIENT
This is a **~30% revenue customer** (~AUD 3.6m). Seller offers **reasonable endeavours** and treats consent as satisfied **on delivery** of the counterparty's written consent. Our position: require **effective consent AND evidence its conditions (clause 11.3) are satisfied before Completion** — not consent-on-delivery, and reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer. The Disclosure Letter §2 confirms **no final consent and no evidence of conditions** exists yet. Make this a hard condition precedent.

## 9. Riverlark (Clause 2/7) — REJECT post-completion release
Seller proposes a release **following Completion**. We require: **current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion.** A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking **plus Frost approval** (not given). Disclosure §3 confirms not repaid / no discharge. Note the ~AUD 3.2m facility bears on the debt-free/cash-free mechanics.

## 10. Employee bonuses (Funds flow / Disclosure §5) — MUST BE ADDRESSED
DD-005 **AUD 420,000** closing bonuses are **excluded from the funds flow** and waved off as "a matter for the Seller." Disclosure §5 also flags **unquantified payroll tax / super / on-costs**. Our position: these plus triggered on-costs must be a **specific line item or seller-funded**; the funds flow must not silently exclude them. Insist on explicit treatment — do not let silence shift this cost to us.

## 11. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1) — TOO NARROW
Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment. We require it **broadened**, while **preserving the SOW3 cure** (DD-004 cl 7.3 — transfer of Project Materials on cleared payment). Disclosure §4 confirms no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment in the data room, and that AUD 180,000 is **not independently verified**. Do not accept the figure as settled either way; broaden the indemnity.

## 12. Export/privacy incident DD-006 (Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6) — PRESERVE, don't dismiss
Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." Correctly, Disclosure §6 confirms **no confirmed breach, scope, harm, notification duty or loss figure**. Consistent with our stance (assume no confirmed breach in either direction), but we should not let "not material" become a disclosed-and-barred matter. Require: **log preservation, investigation, and ongoing updates**, plus a specific indemnity for this incident. Keep it live, not closed.

## 13. Sandbar renewals (Disclosure §8) — ASSESS, don't accept characterisation
Seller labels the three **AUD 330,000** renewals "ordinary-course operating costs." Disclosure §8 admits it does **not** state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Per playbook: **assess independently; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction** — but equally no automatic acceptance as ordinary course. Reserve position pending the underlying terms (DD-008/DD-011).

## 14. Tax / IP — NOT settled
Seller declares these "settled under the general regime." Our playbook keeps **Tax/IP OPEN**, separate from the general regime, with **no unlimited liability and no resolution assumed**. Reject the deemed settlement; keep these categories separate and open.

## 15. Title evidence (Disclosure §10) — INSUFFICIENT
Seller evidences 100% title solely by the **DD-012 share register**. That is a supplied internal source, **not independent proof**. Require **independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence**. Disclosure §10 itself concedes we have not completed our own verification — do so before relying on it.

## 16. Disclosure §1.4 / §11 — note
§1.4 (no admission of breach/liability/requirement) is standard but should not be allowed to undercut the fraud carve-out or specific indemnities. §7 (lease) and §9 (Mossvale) assert no consent is triggered by the share sale — plausible but **verify against DD-007 and DD-009** directly rather than accept the Seller's characterisation.

---

## Summary of Recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller | Our Position / Action |
|---|-------|--------|----------------------|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / 4.8m | Push to **25% / 6.0m**; 20% needs Frost authority (none) |
| 2 | De minimis | 25k | **5k** |
| 2 | Basket | 250k, excess-only | **50k, first-dollar** |
| 3 | Claims period | 18 mths | **24 mths**; reject "all Claims" default sweep |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | same as general | **Separate: 100% cap, 6+ yrs, outside basket/knowledge** |
| 5 | Fraud | absent | **Insert non-waivable carve-out** from all limits |
| 6 | Disclosure | whole-DR + public reg | **Specific fair disclosure only** |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | blanket + constructive | **Delete; actual knowledge, named persons; never title/fraud/indemnity** |
| 8 | Bluefen | reasonable endeavours, on-delivery | **Effective consent + conditions satisfied as CP** |
| 9 | Riverlark | post-completion release | **Repay from Completion funds + release at Completion** |
| 10 | Bonuses (420k) | off funds flow | **Line item or seller-funded + on-costs** |
| 11 | Ironquay | SOW3-only | **Broaden; preserve cure; 180k unverified** |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "not material" | **Preserve/investigate/update + indemnity; no admission either way** |
| 13 | Sandbar (330k) | ordinary course | **Assess; no auto Debt/deduction, no auto acceptance** |
| 14 | Tax / IP | "settled" | **Keep OPEN and separate** |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent evidence required** |

**Top priorities for the mark-up:** (1) reject the `[STANDARD]`/pre-cleared framing in full; (2) restore the separate Fundamental/Title regime and insert the fraud carve-out — these are non-negotiable structural protections; (3) fix the limitation package (cap/basket/de minimis/period) to our baselines; (4) harden Bluefen and Riverlark into real Completion conditions; (5) force the 420k bonuses into the funds flow.

**Authority note:** Three Seller asks (20% cap, 18-month period, post-completion Riverlark release) correspond to fallbacks that require **Amelia Frost's written approval**, which has not been given. I have treated all three as unavailable. If the deal team wants to explore any of them, that approval must be obtained first — I should not concede them on my own initiative.

Want me to draft specific mark-up language for any of these clauses?
